title: Opening sets chosen for the town, like a circus
summary: McRae explains Webb's numbered opening sets, picked for the crowd, and answers Frenchie's complaint with the circus comparison.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: I forget Lionel's road manager. He was probably the same -- It was the same guy. With Louie? Frenchie. Frenchie came over from the -- See, those guys would go from different offices and work -- take the bands out. I think he came over from Glaser's office. But you had a couple of good guys there. But he had a habit of wanting to -- He had said to me one night -- says, "Why do yall open with the same set every night?" Now when you're on the road, we're playing a different town every night, right? Well, with Chick we had like a number one set, a number two set, number three set, number four set. We had a set for Ella -- what she'd (inaudible) open with, you know, what she come on with -- something like that. Then we'd say (Inaudible), "Let's open up with number two," according to what kind of town or crowd we were

(inaudible) crowd is building up, we open up with something -- you know, nice swing. You know, just something (inaudible).
Big crowd, like you get in town and they got two or three thousand just rushing in there ready to go, you know, we open up with some biggies, you know. Something real strong, you know.
Get them in the mood, you know. They come there, they're ready to go. Get us in the mood.
So we'd open up with something real kicking, you know. We'll kick 'em off, right off -- you know, something like that.
So Frenchie say to me, "Why you always play the same numbers every night -- open up with he same numbers?"
I say, "We're in a different town. That's our show. Don't you see the circus open up -- what does a circus do when it comes to town?" (inaudible).

I say, "This is our show! People follow us around. We don't wanna change the set. We got number one, number two (inaudible) that's the set. Even that gets the band in the mood. If they're feeling low, they know these numbers." If you open up with something (inaudible) you haven't been playing for a long time, play that later. Let's open up with something -- We got a number two set, number three set -- well, one of those sets is gonna get you. So that's why they called the sets. We have sets to open up with. That is the whole travelling -- like a show. So they used to tell me -- they say, Well, (inaudible) Teddy. I tell them, I say, "Well, I'm from the big tent. I'm from the school of Chick Webb.
